annotation_description: Playing Plains instead of Island on turn 1 means they cannot hold up Brainstorm, the only 1-mana instant in their hand. Having Island available allows casting Brainstorm at end of an opponent's turn to dig for better cards and set up future draws.

Howling Mine is a symmetrical draw effect that benefits all four opponents equally. In a 4-player game, you draw 1 extra card per turn cycle but your opponents collectively draw 3 extra cards. This is especially bad when played early (turn 3) as it accelerates opponents into their threats and answers. Meanwhile, Jotun Grunt is a 4/4 for 2 mana that applies pressure and can manage graveyards. Additionally, Gem3F Stoic already has a Baleful Strix on board that benefits from extra cards, and DSV3 Spike has Jet Medallion to cast cheaper spells drawn off the Mine.

Casting Skirsdag High Priest first instead of Mind Stone. While both could potentially be cast this turn (total 3 mana needed, 4 available), Mind Stone should be the priority to ensure mana ramp toward Drana on turn 4. Skirsdag High Priest is nearly useless without other creatures and morbid, making it a very low-impact play on its own. If for some reason only one spell gets cast, Mind Stone is clearly better.

DSV3 Spike has 5 lands (including Jet Medallion for cost reduction) and Mind Stone in hand, but chose to pass without playing anything. Mind Stone costs 2 mana and would provide ramp for the expensive cards in hand (Drana at 5 mana, Evernight Shade at 4 mana, Skeletal Scrying). With only 4 lands producing mana plus Jet Medallion, deploying Mind Stone accelerates toward casting Drana or Syr Konrad-level threats a turn earlier. Swiftfoot Boots (also 2 mana) could also be deployed to protect a future Drana. There's no reason to hold mana open with no instants worth casting at this point in the game (Skeletal Scrying with X=0 is useless, and Black Sun's Zenith for X=0 or X=1 isn't needed yet).

Cycling Miscalculation instead of making a land drop on Turn 3 with an extremely mana-hungry hand (Damnation, Cryptic Command, Mystical Teachings, Sylvan Library). Missing land drops delays all these powerful spells.

Gem3F Stoic has Krosan Grip in hand and MiMo Vorthos has Howling Mine on the battlefield, which benefits all opponents equally. Destroying Howling Mine with Krosan Grip (which has split second, so it can't be responded to) would deny card advantage to all three opponents while Stoic already has a strong hand with Damnation, Cryptic Command, Mystical Teachings, and Miscalculation. Instead, they chose to cast Sylvan Library, which is a strong card but could have been played next turn after removing Howling Mine. However, Sylvan Library is excellent and playing it early maximizes its value over time, and Howling Mine does also give Stoic extra draws. The decision is defensible but debatable - Howling Mine helping three opponents vs. one player is generally bad for the table, and Stoic already has a full hand.

DSV3 Spike cast Ob Nixilis of the Black Oath without first playing Myriad Landscape. Since Myriad Landscape enters tapped, playing it first costs nothing and provides future ramp value. Playing spells before lands risks forgetting the land drop entirely.

Playing Snow-Covered Island leaves Gem3F unable to cast Damnation (needs BB) this turn or next without another black source. With threats building (Ob Nixilis at loyalty, Florian, Jotun Grunt), enabling Damnation should be a priority. Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth would make all lands produce black, immediately enabling Damnation and fixing mana for the rest of the game.

Passed with 10 cards in hand, forcing a discard of 3 cards to hand size. Had 4 untapped lands and could have cast Mystical Teachings (3U) to search for an instant card, converting a card they'd discard anyway into a tutored instant. Also appears to have missed playing a land drop, which would have reduced discards further.

Gem3P Johnny passed without equipping Basilisk Collar to Florian before combat. Florian with first strike + deathtouch (from the Collar) becomes an extremely effective attacker that kills any blocker before it can deal damage back, and lifelink provides life gain. This makes attacking much safer and more profitable.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacking DSV3 Spike at 43 life for 4 damage is low impact. Ob Nixilis of the Black Oath is actively generating value each turn (+2 draining all opponents, or making 5/5 demons). Attacking the planeswalker to reduce its loyalty would deny significant incremental advantage.

Goblin Cadets is a 2/1 for R with the significant downside that whenever it blocks or becomes blocked, an opponent gains control of it. In a multiplayer game, this creature is almost always a liability - it can't attack profitably into any board with blockers without giving itself away, and it can't block without the same problem. Meanwhile, Soul Snare (W enchantment that can exile an attacking creature) provides defensive value, and Windborn Muse (3W flying 2/3 that taxes attackers) would be castable next turn and provides much better board presence. Crescendo of War (3W) is also available and could be impactful. Playing a creature that will likely be given away to an opponent seems low-value compared to deploying Soul Snare for 1 mana, which provides immediate defensive utility.

chosen_display: Ob Nixilis of the Black Oath
annotation_description: DSV3 Spike had enough mana to both activate Myriad Landscape (fetching two basic Swamps tapped) and cast Drana with Jet Medallion's discount, but skipped the Landscape activation. This missed free ramp - they would have had 6 mana sources next turn instead of 5 (with Landscape still needing activation later).

Sensei's Divining Top is a powerful repeatable card selection engine that becomes very difficult to remove once it resolves. Letting it resolve gives the opponent sustained incremental advantage for the rest of the game.

Failed to play Island from hand, missing a land drop. With expensive spells in hand (Damnation at 4 mana, Cryptic Command at 4 mana, Mystical Teachings at 4 mana, Intuition at 3 mana), getting to 6 available lands is important for holding up multiple options or casting spells with protection mana. At 27 life facing multiple threats including Ob Nixilis and Florian, maximizing mana development is critical.

message: Put two cards from a single graveyard on the bottom of their owner's library, Put two cards from a single graveyard on the bottom of their owner's library?
annotation_description: Jotun Grunt's upkeep trigger requires putting 2 cards from a single graveyard on bottom of library. MiMo chose to target a graveyard with only basic lands instead of Gem3F Stoic's graveyard which contains Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth - a powerful land that could be recurred.

Attacking Gem3P Johnny at 39 life when Ob Nixilis of the Black Oath (3 loyalty) is on DSV3 Spike's board generating significant value each turn. Ob Nixilis can drain life or create 5/5 flying demons. Additionally, Gem3P Johnny has Florian (3/3 first strike) available to block, making attacks less efficient. Attacking into first strike with Goblin Cadets also risks losing it to the 'becomes blocked' trigger.

Ob Nixilis of the Black Oath is generating recurring value (draining life, creating 5/5 demons) and is likely the most dangerous permanent on the board. Combustible Gearhulk's ETB has already resolved, so it's just a 6/6 body. Both targets give their owner 2 cards from Oblation, but removing the planeswalker prevents ongoing value generation.

Gem3F Stoic passed priority during combat without activating Sensei's Divining Top. With no mana being used this turn and the Top available, they could have activated it to look at the top 3 cards and rearrange them, which is essentially free information gathering that costs only 1 mana. This is especially relevant since they have Sylvan Library and will want to optimize their draw step. Additionally, with Wooded Foothills uncracked, they could use Top first to see what's on top, then decide whether to shuffle with the fetchland. Passing up a free Top activation at end of opponent's turn is a missed opportunity.

Gem3F Stoic passed priority at end of turn without using Sensei's Divining Top's activated ability ({1}: Look at the top three cards) or cracking Wooded Foothills. With mana available (Underground Sea, Snow-Covered Island, Creeping Tar Pit all untapped) and no pressing need to hold up all mana, activating Sensei's Divining Top at end of opponent's turn to arrange the top 3 cards is nearly free and provides valuable information for the Sylvan Library draw step. This is a consistent value engine that should be used whenever possible at end of turn.

During the combat phase (likely an opponent's end step or similar timing window), Gem3F Stoic declined to activate Sensei's Divining Top to look at the top 3 cards of their library. This is a free information advantage that should almost always be used when mana is available, especially before their own draw step with Sylvan Library on the battlefield. Knowing the top 3 cards helps make optimal Sylvan Library decisions. They have an untapped Snow-Covered Island and other untapped lands to pay the {1} activation cost.

Failed to activate Sensei's Divining Top before Sylvan Library trigger resolves. Top + Sylvan Library is a classic synergy: arranging the top 3 cards lets you put the best cards on top to draw and keep, while putting weaker cards in positions where you'll put them back (avoiding the 4 life cost). At 19 life, optimizing Sylvan Library draws is important.

Failed to activate Sensei's Divining Top before Sylvan Library trigger resolves. The Top + Sylvan Library combo is one of the most powerful synergies in Magic: tap Top to draw a card (putting Top on top of library), then Sylvan Library draws Top + another card. Since Top was 'drawn this turn,' you put Top back on top of your library as one of the two cards, effectively drawing an extra card every turn for free with no life payment.

Gem3F Stoic passed their precombat main phase without playing Tolaria West from hand. Missing a land drop when holding expensive spells (Cryptic Command, Damnation, Mystical Teachings, Fact or Fiction) is suboptimal. With only 6 available mana sources and multiple 4-mana spells, getting to 7+ mana is important.

Gem3F Stoic passed on activating Creeping Tar Pit during their own combat phase to deal 3 unblockable damage. With 6 untapped lands, activating Tar Pit (1UB) would leave 3 lands untapped - enough to hold up Miscalculation (1U) though not Cryptic Command (1UUU). In a multiplayer game at 19 life with strong control cards in hand, the trade-off between 3 unblockable damage and keeping Cryptic Command mana open is debatable.

Gem3F Stoic passed with untapped mana and Sensei's Divining Top on board, missing free value from Top's {1} activation to arrange top 3 cards. They also could have cracked Wooded Foothills to thin their deck. Instead they pass and have to discard a card from hand. They could have also cast Fact or Fiction or Intuition to get card selection before discarding, converting the discard into better card quality.

Kardur, Doomscourge is a very dangerous threat against Gem3F Stoic who is at only 19 life. When Kardur enters, all opponents' creatures must attack each combat and must attack a player other than Kardur's controller. This forces Gem3F Stoic's creatures (if any) to attack into unfavorable situations, and more importantly forces other players' creatures to attack Gem3F Stoic (since they can't attack Gem3P Johnny who controls Kardur). With DSV3 Spike having Ob Nixilis capable of making 5/5 demons, and MiMo Vorthos having Jotun Grunt, Gem3F Stoic at 19 life could take significant damage. Gem3F Stoic has Miscalculation in hand which could counter Kardur unless the opponent pays {2}. Gem3P Johnny has only Foreboding Ruins untapped (and Swamp and Mountain untapped), so after casting Kardur for {2}{B}{R} using Temple of the False God + Mountain + Foreboding Ruins + Mountain/Swamp, they likely have limited mana remaining. Looking at Gem3P Johnny's board: Mountain (tapped), Swamp (untapped), Mountain (untapped), Temple of the False God (tapped), Foreboding Ruins (tapped), Rakdos Signet. They cast Kardur for BBRR using some combination. They may have 1-2 mana available to pay for Miscalculation. However, Cryptic Command is also available and cannot be paid around - it would counter Kardur and draw a card. Gem3F has the mana: Underground Sea + Tropical Island + Snow-Covered Island + Island = UUUB or similar, enough for {1}{U}{U}{U}. Letting Kardur resolve when at 19 life with a forced-attack effect is very dangerous.

Punishing Fire dealt 2 damage to Gem3P Johnny at 27 life, which is nearly meaningless in a multiplayer game. Skirsdag High Priest (1/2) was available as a target and is a high-value engine piece that generates 5/5 flying Demons.

By selecting Brainstorm from their own graveyard, MiMo committed to removing cards from their own graveyard for Jotun Grunt's upkeep cost. This means the second card must also come from their graveyard (Oblation or Punishing Fire), losing potential recursion value from Punishing Fire. Punishing Fire can be recurred whenever an opponent gains life (DSV3 Spike has Ob Nixilis which causes life loss/gain effects), making it a valuable graveyard resource.

MiMo Vorthos sacrificed Soul Snare to Perilous Research instead of a tapped land or Howling Mine. Soul Snare is a valuable defensive enchantment that can exile attacking creatures, which is important when at 31 life in a multiplayer game with threats like Ob Nixilis creating 5/5 demons and Florian on the board. Howling Mine benefits all opponents equally and is arguably helping the opponents more than MiMo at this point. Sacrificing a tapped land (like Izzet Boilerworks or the tapped Plains/Mountain) would preserve both defensive options, though losing a land is painful. However, sacrificing Howling Mine would remove symmetric card advantage that benefits all four opponents while keeping Soul Snare as protection.

message: Select a permanent or player for Jotun Grunt to attack (must attack effect)
annotation_description: Attacking DSV3 Spike at 61 life with a 4/1 creature deals negligible damage (4 out of 61). Ob Nixilis of the Black Oath is a high-value planeswalker generating card advantage and 5/5 demons, and attacking it could remove it. Alternatively, Gem3F Stoic at 19 life takes proportionally much more meaningful damage.

Failed to activate Sensei's Divining Top's {1} ability to look at and rearrange the top 3 cards before the Howling Mine extra draw resolves. With Sylvan Library also providing additional draws this turn, arranging the top of the library first would optimize card selection across all draw effects.

Drana, Kalastria Bloodchief is apparently attacking unblocked, and DSV3 Spike has untapped mana available to activate her pump ability ({X}{B}{B}: target creature gets -0/-X, Drana gets +X/+0). Not pumping Drana when she's connecting for free combat damage leaves value on the table.

DSV3 Spike had untapped mana (Polluted Mire, Swamp, Mind Stone, Myriad Landscape = 2B+2C) and could have activated Drana's ability for X=2 targeting Gem3P Johnny's Florian, Voldaren Scion (giving it -0/-2 and Drana +2/+0). This would have dealt 12 total combat damage instead of 10 to Gem3F Stoic (bringing them to 6 instead of 8) while also weakening an opponent's creature, all at no card cost.

At 6 life with Sylvan Library in play and Underground Sea untapped, Gem3F Stoic declined to activate Sensei's Divining Top's {1} look-at-top-3 ability. With only 1 untapped land, they can't cast any of their counterspells (Miscalculation needs 2 mana), so the mana would go to waste. Arranging the top 3 cards is especially valuable with Sylvan Library, letting them optimize their next draw step.

message: Select 2 cards of cards drawn this turn (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: At 1 life with Sylvan Library, Gem3F chose to put Pernicious Deed back on top of their library instead of the much weaker Raven's Crime or Island. Pernicious Deed is a powerful instant-speed board wipe that hits artifacts, creatures, and enchantments - extremely valuable at 1 life for survival. While they have Damnation in hand, Pernicious Deed is more flexible (instant speed, scalable, hits non-creatures).

Gem3F Stoic is at 1 life and passed priority during combat without using Sensei's Divining Top to look at the top 3 cards or activating any abilities. At 1 life, every decision matters critically. While no one appears to be attacking Stoic this combat step specifically, using Sensei's Divining Top to set up draws (especially with Sylvan Library on board) would be free information gathering. However, they may be saving mana for counterspells (Miscalculation) or waiting for end of turn to use Fact or Fiction/Mystical Teachings, which is defensible.

At 1 life, Gem3F cast Mystical Teachings (4 mana) during their own beginning phase before using Sensei's Divining Top to look at top 3 cards first. Using Top's {1} activated ability first would let them see what's available before committing 4 mana, potentially allowing them to hold up Miscalculation or other protection. Additionally, spending 4 mana on their own turn at 1 life leaves minimal mana for countermagic (Miscalculation) during opponents' turns.

Declined to cast Skeletal Scrying for X=1 when they had the mana (1 untapped Swamp after Jet Medallion discount) and a card in the graveyard to exile. At 74 life, the 1 life cost is completely negligible, making this essentially a free card draw.

message: Select card to discard (selected 1 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Selected Geothermal Bog (a BR dual land) as a discard instead of basic Mountain. In a BR deck needing heavy black mana for cards like Syr Konrad (3BB) and Rakdos (BBRR), the dual land is strictly better than a basic Mountain.

Cast Windborn Muse before playing a land drop. With Plains and Mountain in hand, playing a land first would give 9 mana instead of 8, preserving more options for additional spells this turn or holding up interaction like Repulse.

DSV3 Spike declined to cast Skeletal Scrying for X=1 during combat. With Jet Medallion reducing the cost, it would only cost {B} (1 of the 2 untapped Swamps), exile the single Infernal Offering from graveyard, draw 1 card, and lose 1 life (negligible at 73 life). This is essentially free card advantage.

DSV3 Spike had multiple creatures available to attack (Skirsdag High Priest, a Demon Token, Drana Kalastria Bloodchief, and Gray Merchant of Asphodel) but chose 'true' which resulted in skipping the attack entirely. With opponents at 23 and 22 life, attacking with the Demon Token (5/5 flying) and Drana (4/4 flying) would deal significant damage to opponents who are already at low life totals. The Windborn Muse tax only applies to attacking MiMo Vorthos, so attacking Gem3P Johnny with flying creatures would be free. Missing this combat damage is a meaningful mistake.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: MiMo Vorthos attacked DSV3 Spike at 72 life with Windborn Muse (2 power) instead of Gem3P Johnny at 22 life. 2 damage into 72 life is essentially meaningless (2.8%), while 2 damage into 22 life (9.1%) puts real pressure on Johnny and brings them closer to lethal range.

Failed to activate Myriad Landscape to search for two basic Swamps. DSV3 Spike had the mana available (2 untapped Swamps to pay the {2} cost) and no better use for the mana. Getting two extra lands would significantly help cast expensive cards in hand like Morkrut Banshee, Syr Konrad, Gray Merchant, etc. Myriad Landscape is a one-time use ability that should be activated as soon as practical.

Liliana's Reaver is a reasonable threat, but Drana, Kalastria Bloodchief is likely stronger in this position. Drana is a 4/4 flyer (better evasion than fear since Florian is black and can block Reaver) and her activated ability serves as repeatable removal that can handle Florian or other threats. With opponents at 22 life each and DSV3 at 72, the game isn't about racing - it's about board control, where Drana excels.

DSV3 Spike passed their precombat main phase without casting anything, with confused reasoning about 'Liliana's Reaver on the stack' (which doesn't exist in hand or battlefield). They had mana available to cast Commander's Sphere (ramping for future turns), Read the Bones (card advantage), or Evernight Shade before combat. Playing Commander's Sphere precombat would provide an additional mana source for post-combat plays.

DSV3 Spike has priority during the Howling Mine trigger resolution at the beginning of the draw step, with mana available. Skeletal Scrying is an instant that could be cast at end of opponent's turn to use mana efficiently, and Myriad Landscape could be activated to thin the deck and ramp. While passing here isn't terrible, activating Myriad Landscape (2 mana + tap + sacrifice) to fetch two Swamps would be pure value - ramping and thinning the deck at no real cost during an opponent's turn when the mana would otherwise go unused. With 72 life, there's no pressure concern, but missing free mana development is a small inefficiency.

DSV3 Spike passed without activating Myriad Landscape, missing free ramp. They have the {2} available to activate it (untapped lands + Mind Stone), and getting two extra Swamps would help cast expensive spells like Morkrut Banshee, Drana, or fuel larger Skeletal Scrying/Black Sun's Zenith later. There's no reason to hold Myriad Landscape.

DSV3 Spike chose to bottom Pestilence Demon and keep Sol Ring on top during the Read the Bones scry. While Sol Ring is excellent, the player already has 8 mana sources on board (including Jet Medallion for black cost reduction and Mind Stone). Sol Ring's impact is diminished at this stage of the game. Pestilence Demon, on the other hand, is a 7/6 flyer that deals 1 damage to each creature and player for {B} each activation - this is extremely powerful with the player at 72 life, especially as a board control tool and win condition. With Jet Medallion reducing the cost, Pestilence Demon would cost 7 generic + 1 black (effectively 7 total with medallion), which is castable soon. The player is drawing 2 cards after scry anyway, so they could have bottomed Sol Ring and kept Pestilence Demon on top to draw it immediately.

Cast Commander's Sphere (a mana rock) when already at 7+ mana sources, without first playing a land from hand (Arcane Lighthouse or Everglades were available). At this stage of the game, additional ramp is less impactful than removing threats. Florian, Voldaren Scion is generating card advantage for Gem3P Johnny each turn.

DSV3 Spike cast Morkrut Banshee before playing a land. They have Arcane Lighthouse in hand which could have been played first for free, providing an additional mana source for the rest of the turn (useful for potential follow-up plays or responses). Additionally, the reasoning references targeting Syr Konrad which isn't on the battlefield, suggesting some confusion about the board state.

Syr Konrad, the Grim (5/4) is a far more dangerous threat than Guard Gomazoa (1/3 defender). Konrad deals 1 damage to each opponent whenever a creature dies, and DSV3 Spike has Black Sun's Zenith in hand - casting it with Konrad on the board would result in massive damage to DSV3 Spike from all the creature deaths. The -4/-4 from Morkrut Banshee would kill Syr Konrad (making it 1/0). Guard Gomazoa is merely a defensive blocker that can't attack.

The player plans to play Blackcleave Cliffs AND Shivan Gorge in the same turn, but can only play one land per turn. Playing Blackcleave Cliffs (which enters tapped with 3+ other lands) instead of Shivan Gorge means they cannot activate Shivan Gorge to deal damage to opponents, which is needed to enable casting Rakdos, Lord of Riots. Without Shivan Gorge's activation, Rakdos cannot be cast this turn since no opponent has lost life yet.

Gem3P Johnny declined to attack with Florian, Voldaren Scion (3/3 first strike) and Goblin Cadets against MiMo Vorthos at 14 life. MiMo Vorthos has no untapped creatures to block. Florian's postcombat main phase trigger depends on opponents losing life this turn - by not attacking, Johnny misses both damage and the ability to look at cards with Florian's trigger. With DSV3 Spike at 68 life and being the main threat, pressuring the weakened MiMo Vorthos (14 life) is important. Additionally, Florian dealing combat damage would enable casting Rakdos, Lord of Riots from hand, which requires an opponent to have lost life this turn. Johnny also has Fear of Burning Alive in hand which could finish off MiMo Vorthos. The reasoning text shows frustration about game engine issues rather than strategic analysis.

message: Choose spell or ability to playSulfurous Springs
chosen_display: 2. {T}: Add {B}. Sulfurous Springs deals 1 damage to you.
annotation_description: Tapped Sulfurous Springs for {B} taking 1 damage when {C} would have sufficed. The {C} could pay for Rakdos Signet's activation cost ({1}), with Signet producing {B}{R}, Swamp producing {B}, and Mountain producing {R}, totaling {B}{B}{R}{R} for Rakdos without any life loss.

MiMo Vorthos has an Island in hand and appears to have not yet played a land this turn (or at least has the option to play it). At 10 life with expensive cards like Death by Dragons (6 mana) and Crescendo of War (4 mana) in hand, missing a land drop is a real cost. Having 9 mana sources next turn instead of 8 could be the difference between deploying a critical spell on time.

Playing Canyon Slough (enters tapped) instead of Swamp (enters untapped) when they have Sol Ring to cast and want to maximize mana for post-combat plays with Florian's trigger and potential Rakdos discount. The extra untapped mana could matter for casting more spells this turn.

Gem3P Johnny has Fear of Burning Alive (4/4) and other attackers against MiMo Vorthos at 10 life. MiMo's board is all tapped lands and a Howling Mine - no blockers whatsoever. Fear of Burning Alive (4) + Florian (3) + Goblin Cadets (2) = 9 damage, putting MiMo to 1. Even just Fear of Burning Alive + Florian = 7 damage to put MiMo to 3. Instead, Johnny skipped the attack entirely, apparently confused by Propaganda-like effects (though MiMo doesn't appear to control one - the Windborn Muse is in MiMo's graveyard). This was a missed opportunity to eliminate or nearly eliminate a player with no blockers.

Chose Mode 2 (destroy all enchantments) which hits nothing meaningful on the board, while Mode 3 (destroy creatures CMC ≤ 3) would have killed Florian, Voldaren Scion (CMC 3), a significant threat from Johnny. At 9 life, removing a 3/3 first striker that could be equipped with Basilisk Collar (deathtouch + lifelink) is important.
